reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses a clustering-to-ordering transition under high compressive strain in a different composition (Al0.1CrCoFeNi), not SRO enhancement by annealing. E2 concerns a BCC W-based refractory alloy, not FCC Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni, and its radiation resistance is linked to second-phase particles and point defect mobilities, not SRO. No evidence is provided for the claimed property improvements or the baseline SRO state.
premises: Annealing near-equiatomic FCC Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni at 800–900 K enhances short-range chemical order (SRO).
Enhanced SRO lowers the free energy of the FCC solid solution, stabilizing it against secondary phases.
Enhanced SRO improves high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, oxidation resistance, and cryogenic toughness.
Rapidly quenched alloys have minimal SRO and are more susceptible to secondary phase nucleation.
